comparison: Perfect alignment on survival analysis claims (C23-C28). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the statistical framework and identification of 14 OS-associated TCs, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming the permutation analysis and prognostic associations as convincing.

Strong agreement on TC121's biological interpretation as synaptic signaling (C47-C54, C66). Both evaluations find the molecular characterization compelling, with peer reviewers explicitly stating the biological interpretation is convincing and the detection of synaptic signaling is supported.

High concordance on spatial transcriptomics validation (C59-C62, C68). Both support the spatial localization findings, though OpenEval notes the inference about unannotated cells being neurons (C61) is speculative. Peer reviewers find the spatial detection compelling and supporting further mechanistic follow-up.

Agreement on c-ICA methodology and primary results (C11-C12, C18-C22). OpenEval supports the quantitative metrics and statistical thresholds, while peer reviewers affirm the innovative methodology and solid data-driven description with detailed documentation.

Concordance on survival tree analysis and TC121's prognostic significance (C29-C35). Both evaluations support the statistical approach and identification of TC121 as the most significant discriminator, with peer reviewers treating the association as established.

Agreement on c-ICA methodology (C11-C12). OpenEval finds the approach well-cited and established, while peer reviewers acknowledge c-ICA as a novel approach allowing identification of subtle transcriptional patterns.

Concordance on cross-study projections and TME interpretation (C55-C58, C70). Both support the validation across cancer types and the interpretation that TC121 represents a TME signal, with peer reviewers accepting the deconvolution interpretation.

Agreement on mechanistic interpretation of TC121's activity patterns (C71-C76). Both find the reasoning logical regarding differential activity in cell lines versus patient samples supporting TME origin, with peer reviewers accepting this interpretation.

Concordance on biological characterization of OS-associated TCs (C40-C46). Both support the gene set enrichment associations and chromosomal characterizations, with peer reviewers treating these as part of the solid data-driven analysis.
Agreement on spatial patterns of TC activity (C63-C65). Both find the localization patterns biologically plausible, with peer reviewers accepting these as part of the comprehensive characterization.

Concordance on characterization of OS-associated TCs (C36-C38). Both support the chromosomal locations and survival associations, with peer reviewers accepting these findings as part of the comprehensive analysis.

Agreement on independent validation of TC166 (C39). Both evaluations support this finding, with OpenEval noting appropriate statistical correction and peer reviewers treating it as part of robust validation.
Concordance on TC121 distribution across cancer subtypes (C34-C35). Both support the observation that all subtypes show elevated TC121 activity, contributing to understanding of generalizability.

Partial divergence on mechanistic conclusions about TC121 (C66-C69, C77, C102-C103). OpenEval supports the synthesis of findings while noting TME origin requires further validation. Peer reviewers accept descriptive findings but explicitly state the study is non-mechanistic and requires experimental validation, expressing reservations about mechanistic conclusions.

Divergence on main conclusions (C102-C103). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported though mechanistic details remain speculative. Peer reviewers accept the descriptive findings but emphasize the study is non-mechanistic and requires experimental validation for mechanistic claims.

Agreement on literature contextualization regarding tumor innervation (C77-C81). Both support the connection to established literature, with peer reviewers accepting this as appropriate background. OpenEval notes the specific mechanistic connection requires further investigation.

Concordance on therapeutic implications and BDNF distinction (C82-C85). Both support the therapeutic landscape discussion and the observation that BDNF is not prominent in TC121, with peer reviewers accepting the speculative nature of therapeutic implications.

Agreement on sensory innervation literature review (C86-C90). Both support the contextualization with appropriate citations, with OpenEval noting the connection to TC121 is speculative but reasonably inferred. Peer reviewers accept this as appropriate discussion.

Concordance on substance P signaling discussion (C91-C95). Both support the distinction from TC121 and the observation that TAC1/TACR1-containing TCs are not survival-associated, strengthening TC121's novelty.

Agreement on therapeutic opportunities discussion (C96-C101). Both support the literature-based discussion of potential therapeutic approaches, with peer reviewers accepting the speculative nature requiring future validation.

OpenEval evaluated background claims on HGSOC epidemiology, treatment, and outcomes (C1-C6) as well-supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory background claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims establishing study rationale regarding bulk transcriptome limitations (C7-C10) as appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these motivational claims.
OpenEval evaluated data collection and preprocessing claims (C13-C17) as clearly documented with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
